feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is stated for it. Iterations 0 and 1 both ended off track at 11-16% progress with max_error of 0.061-0.070 m and one line-loss event per run (iteration 0 and iteration 1 outcome tables). Changing the drivetrain (track 0.12 to 0.10 m, mass 0.8 to 0.6 kg) moved the score only from 52.18 to 52.33, so drivetrain is not what limits the run. This candidate tests the sensor lead alone, moving y from 0.05 to 0.07 m, with the controller unchanged. Depending on what the race shows: if progress rises on the oval and s-bend and max_error falls below 0.06 m, keep y = 0.07 m. If slalom steering_oscillation rises clearly above the iteration 1 level of about 0.15 while max_error falls, the lead is overshooting, so use y = 0.065 m. If progress and max_error are within about 0.01 of iterations 0 and 1, the lead is not the constraint and the next change should be to the wheel or sensor spacing rather than to the lead again.
requested_changes: If lead y = 0.07 m raises progress on the oval and s-bend with max_error below 0.06 m, keep y = 0.07 m. If slalom steering_oscillation rises above about 0.16 (iteration 1 slalom level 0.154), try y = 0.065 m to limit overshoot, citing the iteration 1 oscillation data.

If progress stays at 11-16% with max_error still near 0.06-0.07 m and line_loss_events still 1, the sensing lead is not the limit. Next try wheel_radius 0.035 m, because no iteration has tested speed or wheel size and iteration 0 and 1 gave no completions.

If line_loss_events rise above 1 at the larger errors seen near the limit, reduce the sensor spacing from 0.015 m to 0.01 m (x = +/-0.02 m) so the outer sensors stay on the tape, citing the iteration 1 telemetry on line loss at max_error 0.06-0.07 m.
